summary: 2D screening label: not_2d_applicable. Studio did not run (simulation status skipped; simulation_allowed=false). The gate failed on input validity: a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, but the floorplan is empty and power_w is {}. The scenario is a custom 2D steady request for a paper whose source is steady 3D conjugate CFD (ANSYS Icepak/FLUENT, realizable k-epsilon) of a staggered circular pin-fin aluminium heat sink cooling a single 2.2 x 2.2 x 0.1 cm chip at a constant 8 W, with 0.1 m/s inlet air at 298 K. Because it is steady, there is no transient trace and no power time series. No bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace case, source commit, or generated-placement input.flp/input.ptrace was used or produced. comparison_valid=false, so no numerical comparison with the paper's 125.50 degC Table 6 maximum source temperature is made, and nothing here replicates the paper. Qualitatively, the paper's temperature is governed by fin geometry, arrangement, forced-convection flow and the heat sink path, which a 2D chip-floorplan conduction model cannot represent. Any Studio result would show only sensitivity to its own package and boundary assumptions, not the paper's. The mismatches that block comparison are: the paper's 3D conjugate forced-air CFD versus a 2D Studio model; the paper's finned-sink convective boundary versus an unspecified Studio cooling and package stack; the paper's single chip with no placement coordinates versus a required floorplan; the paper's maximum over the source versus any Studio aggregation; and the paper's steady regime, which is the same regime a custom 2D steady run would use, though its geometry and flow are not representable. Independent review items (page/asset locators, methods, code, parameters, config and data checks) are also unresolved, and no linked assets exist.

Full 3D conjugate CFD of an air-cooled pin-fin heat sink in a cabinet, with a 3D solid heat sink, fins and a fluid domain. A 2D steady chip floorplan model cannot represent fin geometry, forced convection, pressure drop or flow-path effects.

The cooling solution is forced-air convection (0.1 m/s inlet, turbulence model, pressure outlet) through a finned aluminium sink. A conduction-only or generic Studio package/cooling model does not reproduce this.

The paper models a single chip with a single 8 W source, so there is no multi-chiplet floorplan, no interposer and no stacked-die structure. Chiplet or interposer placement optimisation is not applicable.
No optimizer or controller exists in the source; the study compares four fixed designs. Optimizer and controller behaviour cannot be replicated or compared.
The workload is steady and constant, with no transient behaviour and no power time series, so a transient trace is not the paper's setup.

The heat sink dimensions are inconsistent within the paper (Table 1: 4x4x1.7 cm; text: 3x3.5x2 cm; fin height 1.5 cm and radius 0.16 cm in the text vs D=0.2 cm in Table 1). The geometry is therefore ambiguous.

The paper's own text conflicts on the flow regime: the assumptions list laminar flow but the model uses realizable k-epsilon. The paper also states constant properties, no radiation and no gravity. The reported solver/model is thus internally ambiguous, and no reliability analysis is performed.

No Studio package/material assumption is taken from the paper, because no Studio bundle was supplied in the packet. Any bundled Studio package/material stack (e.g. layer materials, TIM, heat sink or ambient boundary) is a separate assumption and is not derived from the paper.

Any 2D placement or one-row power trace built by the runner would be illustrative only: its coordinates and the 8 W power would be kept separate from paper-derived facts, and its temperatures must not be compared numerically with the paper's 125.50 C.

The paper provides only the chip footprint (2.2 x 2.2 x 0.1 cm) and total power (8 W), with no placement coordinates for a floorplan, so a complete floorplan with x_m/y_m is not paper-derived; the floorplan is left empty.
